subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finsecure.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up

Hi Oliver,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking through FinSecure’s use cases. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of needs (from our call):
- Sensitive PII and transaction data must never egress to public networks.
- Customer-managed KMS for encryption keys is required.
- Audit logs and long-term retention (7+ years) for access logs.
- Pen-test / vulnerability scan evidence required during procurement.
- Potential on-prem requirement for certain regulatory workloads (scope TBD).

What this means for deployment mode:
- Hosted API: fast, but not appropriate if you require customer-managed VPC/KMS or strict no-egress guarantees.
- Dedicated capacity: provides reserved GPU pools and tenant isolation but runs in Redwood-managed network — we can restrict egress and offer dedicated capacity, but customer KMS and full VPC peering are not automatic.
- Private VPC / On-prem: designed for the strictest controls — customer-managed VPC (no public egress), KMS integrations, and an on-prem package for air-gapped needs.

Immediate asks from our side so we can scope:
1) Can you confirm which workloads need absolute no-egress (vs. acceptable within-peer egress to specific endpoints)?
2) Do you have an existing customer KMS (Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS / HSM) you prefer?
3) Any strict timeline / procurement milestones we should map to (SOW, pen-test windows)?

Next steps I propose: schedule a technical call with Mateo (SE) + your security/infra lead to iron out the network/KMS requirements and proposed SOW. I’ve attached our high-level security checklist and a one-pager comparing Dedicated vs Private VPC.

Proposed times: I’m available Tue/Wed next week 10–12 PT; here’s my scheduler: https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/30min

Attachments: (attachment: redwood-security-checklist.pdf, type: application/pdf), (attachment: dedicated-vs-private-vpc-one-pager.pdf, type: application/pdf)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: FinSecure - Security Team <security@finsecure.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. Correct on the main points. A few clarifications from security: 

- We require customer-managed VPC with no internet egress for the production tenant. Admin and monitoring traffic may be routed via a management VPC but must be documented and approved.
- Keys must be customer-controlled (AWS KMS or HSM). We cannot accept Redwood-managed keys for production sensitive workloads.
- Audit logs must be exported to our SIEM (Splunk) and retained per policy (7 years).
- SOC 2 Type II evidence + recent pentest report are required to move forward with procurement — ideally before the SOW phase.
- On-prem is on the table for ~20% of workload (legacy batch jobs) — we’ll need a clear statement of work and timeline if we choose that path.

Can you provide an initial ballpark for incremental cost and expected lead time for Private VPC vs Dedicated capacity with the above constraints? Also please share the SOC 2 report and any pen-test summary you can at this stage.

Oliver
Director, Infrastructure Security
FinSecure
oliver.grant@finsecure.com | (202) 555-4172
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finsecure.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T13:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up

Thanks Oliver — this is super helpful. Quick answers and proposed plan: 

1) Customer-managed VPC with no internet egress is supported under our Private VPC offering. We’ll map the exact egress/peer endpoints during the technical call.
2) Customer KMS: we support AWS KMS and external HSM integrations with Private VPC; for Dedicated capacity we can support customer KMS in many configurations but it requires additional network setup and an implementation timeline.
3) SOC 2 + pen-test: I’ve attached a redacted SOC 2 summary and our security checklist; Mateo is looping in the SE/SRE team to prepare a checklist of additional evidence and an estimated timeline for an on-prem deployment.

Ballpark economics (very high level):
- Dedicated capacity (Redwood-managed network, reserved GPUs): lower setup lead time (2–4 weeks), lower monthly commitment vs full Private VPC, but limited in-cust KMS options and less strict network isolation by default.
- Private VPC (customer-managed VPC or customer-hosted on-prem): higher setup (4–8+ weeks depending on approvals/ops), higher one-time engineering & recurring infra costs, meets strict no-egress/KMS requirements.

Next step: Mateo and I can run a 45min technical scoping call to capture exact network flows, KMS type, SIEM endpoints, and a draft SOW. Mateo — can you share availability (next Tue/Thu) and we’ll send a calendar invite to Oliver + security team?

I’m also attaching an editable draft MAP (mutual action plan) to help track procurement milestones.

Attachments: (attachment: finsecure-mrp-draft.docx, type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Thanks,
Marissa
